title: CPB Registry Entry
description: Machine-checkable shape for one CPB registry submission (Payload Canonicalization Algorithm Registry or Artifact Type Registry). Fill in registry/entries/TEMPLATE.yaml, save it as registry/entries/<name>.yaml, and open a PR — .github/validate_registry_entries.py validates every file under registry/entries/ against this schema and, for any entry that declares in-repo vectors, executes them and rejects the entry if they do not run clean. This schema is the machine-checkable half of the fill-in template; REGISTRY.md's Entry Template section remains the normative prose description of every field. The seven questions this schema exists to force an answer to (construction-as-data: digest-input bytes, exclusions, canonicalization profile, hash, representation; composite-or-not; cross-language parity proven by vectors) are asked verbatim as property descriptions on `seven_questions` below.

name.description: The controlled identifier this entry registers — the token that will appear in a `type` field (Artifact Type Registry) or as an algorithm id (Payload Canonicalization Algorithm Registry). Lowercase, hyphen-separated.

target_registry.description: Which of CPB's two registries (draft §13.1 / §13.2) this entry targets.

rung.description: Registration Ladder rung (REGISTRY.md). 'reserved' is the pre-registration name hold described there — not a lifecycle status — and is the only rung that may omit seven_questions/digest_contexts/fixtures entirely.

status.description: REGISTRY.md Entry Status Vocabulary term, used verbatim. Must be consistent with `rung` (owner_authored -> owner-confirmed; third_party_documented -> third-party-documented; provisional -> provisional; reserved -> reserved).

reference.description: Publicly available specification: Internet-Draft, RFC, or a repository reference. A repository reference MUST include a commit hash — a branch or tag alone is not a pin.

owner.description: The artifact/algorithm owner. For a `provisional` entry filed ahead of owner confirmation, name the owner anyway (e.g. the org whose spec is being read) so the record shows who is being asked to confirm.

self_attestation.description: Third-Party Registration Rule 2: "Registered by X from Y at commit Z."

registrant.description: Required when rung is third_party_documented. Omit for owner_authored, provisional, and reserved entries.

disclosure.description: Required prose statement when the owner or confirmer also holds a CPB editor or draft co-author role (REGISTRY.md Required Fields table). No CI check can detect when this applies — that is a human/DE judgment call, stated here so the schema does not imply otherwise.

de_reviewer.description: Designated Expert assigned to this entry, or the literal string 'TBD' with a one-line reason (e.g. awaiting the third designated-expert appointment).

open_questions.description: Explicit unresolved items a Designated Expert or the owner must settle before this entry can promote. Required key (may be an empty array for a fully-settled owner-confirmed entry) so a reviewer never has to infer whether something was simply forgotten versus deliberately left open. CPB editors MUST NOT resolve one of these on the owner's/DE's behalf — see REGISTRY.md's 'CPB editors MUST NOT fill in owner-supplied fields' rule.

seven_questions.description: The registration template's core content, in the form the questions were put to registrants: construction-as-data (five parts), composite-or-not, and cross-language parity. Required for every rung except 'reserved'.

digest_input_bytes.description: Q1 — What exact bytes is the digest computed over? Name the field set (or, under as-transmitted, the cited named production / byte-boundary selector), not just the containing message.

exclusion_set.description: Q2 — Which fields (if any) are excluded from that byte sequence before digesting? Write 'none' explicitly rather than leaving this blank — blank and 'none' are not the same claim.

canonicalization_profile.description: Q3 — Which canonicalization profile applies? Name a token already in the Payload Canonicalization Algorithm Registry (registry.json / REGISTRY.md §Payload Canonicalization Algorithm Registry), or state 'TBD — new algorithm token proposed: <name>' / 'TBD — Designated Expert must choose' if none fits yet. Naming an algorithm family ("JCS") is not an answer; the answer names one registered token.

hash_algorithm.description: Q4 — What hash function? Normally pinned by the canonicalization-profile token itself (e.g. every currently registered token is SHA-256) — state it anyway so this entry is self-contained and a mismatch with the named profile is visible on inspection.

representation.description: Q5 — How is the digest output represented? e.g. '64-char lowercase hex', 'sha256: + 64-char lowercase hex', 'raw 32 octets'. Two representations of the same bytes are not interchangeable (see REGISTRY.md's machine-mandate discriminating vector) — state the exact one.

is_composite.description: Q6a — Does this artifact type embed other registered artifact types or CPB-digested payloads inside itself?

statement.description: Q6b — Composite payloads are NEVER inlined verbatim inside a signed record; a composite member is carried as a typed digest REFERENCE (CPB §6-style {type, digest_alg, digest}) inside the signed record, never a copy of the referenced bytes. If is_composite is true, state which field(s) carry the reference and confirm no member field embeds another artifact's payload bytes directly. If is_composite is false, a one-line confirmation that this type carries no other registered artifact type by reference or by value is sufficient.

Q7 — Cross-language/cross-implementation parity is demonstrated by VECTORS producing byte-identical pre-images and digests across independent implementations, never by one implementer reading another's source. State how many independent implementations this entry's vectors have been run against, or 'not yet demonstrated — N/A, single implementation to date' if only one exists.

implementations.description: Independent implementations the parity statement above is claiming agreement across, if any.

digest_contexts.description: Optional richer breakdown for an entry with more than one digest context (purpose identifier/equivalence, multiple profile versions, etc — see the agent-action-capsule and machine-mandate entries in REGISTRY.md for worked examples). When present, seven_questions may say 'see digest_contexts[]' instead of repeating per-context detail. Shape matches registry.json's own digest_contexts (registry_schema.json) so a promoted entry's data does not need reshaping.

fixtures.description: Required conformance vector set (Registration Rule 2: positive AND negative, both directions). Required for owner_authored and third_party_documented rungs. A provisional entry MAY omit this entirely (that incompleteness is exactly what keeps it at Rung 3) — but if it declares vectors_dir anyway, those vectors are still mechanically checked.

vectors_dir.description: Path, relative to the repository root, to this entry's vectors IN THIS REPO. If present, .github/validate_registry_entries.py runs .github/check_vectors.py against it and REJECTS the entry if any vector fails to execute cleanly (nonzero FAILED count) or is not two-sided (no positive or no must_fail case), unless external_vector_set below applies instead.

positive.description: Vector case ids or file paths carrying pinned expected values.

boundary.description: Vector case ids or file paths at the construction's edge cases (e.g. empty field set, smallest legal instance).

negative.description: MUST-FAIL vector case ids or file paths. Registration Rule 2: positives-only cannot detect an implementation that is too permissive.

external_vector_set.description: Third-Party Registration Rule 4: cite the owner's own published vector set rather than fabricating one. Exempts this entry from local in-repo execution (validate_registry_entries.py cannot run another repository's test suite) but the citation must be commit-pinned.

discriminating_vector.description: Gate A: a conformance case (positive or MUST-FAIL) that distinguishes this entry from every currently registered neighbour in the same registry table, both directions. See REGISTRY.md Designated Expert Admission Checklist, Gate A.

consuming_profile.description: Gate B: at least one spec-revision-pinned reference to a specification or deployment that uses this registered name normatively. The entry's own specification does not count.

notes.description: Free-text notes for the CPB editor — non-normative.
